title: Pace Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Pace Calculator: Running pace, speed and race finish time. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Pace Calculator](/pace-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Running pace, speed and race finish time. Enter your distance, hours, minutes and seconds and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Pace is the time it takes to cover one kilometre or mile. Knowing it helps you train at the right effort and plan race targets. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Health & Fitness tools include [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator), [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) and [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator).

## How to use the Pace Calculator

Start by entering your distance (km), then entering your hours, entering your minutes and finally entering your seconds. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your distance (km).
2. Enter your hours.
3. Enter your minutes.
4. Enter your seconds.
5. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
6. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Pace = total time ÷ distance. Speed = distance ÷ time.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Pace Calculator](/pace-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 10 km in 55:00 is a pace of 5:30 per km (8:51 per mile), or 10.91 km/h. Try the same figures in the [Pace Calculator](/pace-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Distance: 10 km, Hours: 0, Minutes: 55, Seconds: 0), the [Pace Calculator](/pace-calculator) returns Pace: 5:30 /km, Pace per mile: 8:51 /mi, Speed: 10.91 km/h, Marathon at this pace: 3h 52m. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Run most training miles at an easy, conversational pace.
- Start races slightly slower than goal pace.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good 5K time?

For recreational runners, 25–30 minutes is common; under 20 minutes is considered fast. Try it with your own numbers in the [Pace Calculator](/pace-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How do I convert min/km to min/mile?

Multiply by 1.609. Try it with your own numbers in the [Pace Calculator](/pace-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Pace Calculator use?

Pace = total time ÷ distance. Speed = distance ÷ time. You can see it in action in the [Pace Calculator](/pace-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Pace Calculator?

Just Distance, Hours, Minutes and Seconds. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
